en: Now, besides large language models, we also
have so-called small language models. And
this is kind of a semi-official term because
in the end, it's the same
but smaller. Because you have to understand
that large language models are called large
language models
because they have lots of parameters, lots
of these numbers in a neural network.
Modern models have billions and trillions of
parameters.
Therefore, they require very powerful
hardware to run them. You can't run these
latest top models on your computer. No
chance, no matter how good it is.
Small language models are the same things,
but with less parameters, far less
parameters.
That allows you to potentially run them on
your machine. You still need a quite good
machine, But it's not totally impossible.
The downside, of course, is that these
models are less powerful, though, because it
turns out that the more parameters you have
in your neural network for a large language
model,
the smarter it is, which kind of makes sense
because more parameters in a nutshell means
that it's able to
model more nuances in language and more
details. So that allows it to be smarter,
and a smaller model has less of these
nuances.
But the good thing is that these small
language models, especially when fine-tuned,
which is also something we'll dive in, can
be quite good at specific tasks. They are
not as smart as their large siblings, but
they can be very good at very specific tasks
like summarizing text or categorizing
incoming email or maybe writing code in a
specific programming language.
And that, of course, makes them very
attractive because because they can
potentially run on your device or in your
network, which gives you privacy benefits,
which also means you don't have to pay for
their usage
outside of the hardware and the electricity,
of course. And that's why small language
models also are very important in the
current and modern
AI landscape we have right now.
